summary: A shapefile dropped as loose parts is read as one shapefile. Publishing any part (.shp, .shx, .dbf, .prj,
.cpg by name; the .shp, .shx and .dbf also by the format their bytes probe as) finds the live parts of its
stem in the batch. Once .shp, .shx and .dbf are all present, one SH2 intake-native-derivative job is queued
on the .shp item; convert-native copies each part from object storage, checks its size and SHA-256, and
reads them with the existing shapefile reader. The derivative is kept, enrolled and read on the large
GeoJSON path unchanged. Originals stay as dropped; no ZIP is made.

decisions.D1: Each part stays its own retained original and item; the set is assembled in the geo service's scratch folder from the parts' object keys.
D2: A set is the case's root items with a card whose source is the latest revision of its family and whose
name, folder path kept, is <stem>.<ext> compared without case. A .shp must probe as shapefile, a .shx as
shapefile-index (the probe's own name for it) and a .dbf as dbf; a .prj or .cpg may be any bytes. Two
parts of one extension rest every part probed / not_understood: 'Shapefile part: <stem> has more than one
.dbf (<names>), so its parts are not read together as one shapefile.'
D3: intake-service publish calls queueShapefileSetTx before the draft queue; it takes the file only when its
stem holds a .shp or .shx, so a lone .dbf (or a .dbf before its .shp arrives) keeps today's table path.
Short of a part, every part rests probed / undecided: 'Shapefile part: waiting for .shx of roads.'
Whole: the other parts rest read / undecided 'Read with <stem>.shp as one shapefile.' and the .shp item's
job id is stableUuid of 'shapefile_set:<shp item>:<sorted member SHA-256s>:<attempt>'. Any order gives the
same id; publishing a part again finds the queued job. nativeDerivativeFormat(card, name) gives
shapefile_set for a shapefile card named .shp.
D4: convert-native accepts format shapefile_set with layer and members (extension, sourceId, objectKey,
sha256, bytes). It checks one .shp, .shx and .dbf, at most one .prj and .cpg, the .shp equal to the
request's pins and the total within the source bound; copies each into one folder under the base name
'layer' (the user's stem never becomes a path) checking size and SHA-256; and reads them through the
shapefile ZIP reader's shared body (CRS from .prj or CR1's officer answer, .cpg encoding, windows).
D5: Job input, convert request and lineage gain an additive members array (sourceId, sourceRevision, sha256,
extension), present only for shapefile_set (lineage refine enforces both ways). The sidecar header names
each part's extension and SHA-256. The parent's words add 'Read as one shapefile from its parts: ...'.
A job whose pinned members are no longer the live set (a part added, replaced or doubled) converts and
writes nothing; the publish that changed the set queued its own job.

good.use: SH2's real shapefile ZIP, unpacked in the test into Council_Buildings.shp/.shx/.dbf/.prj/.cpg
orders: prj, cpg, dbf, shp, shx (dbf first among the required parts)
shx, cpg, shp, prj, dbf: same job id

difficult_test_only: two .dbf under one stem (blocks.dbf, Blocks.DBF): every part refused in words, no job
a set short of its .shx: .shp and .dbf wait in words, no job
no .prj: the layer asks the officer (crs_unstated); CR1's answer converts it as officer_stated
a part's SHA-256 differs at copy: refused 'The retained original's size or SHA-256 differs from its receipt.'
a set request short of its .shx, with two .dbf, or with a .shp other than the named original: refused
a file named .shx whose bytes are not a shapefile index: keeps its own path
inputs.unchanged: a lone .dbf is not taken by the set path and gets no draft words (today's table path)
